# Reuse Generated Files For Publish

This is the active follow-on to [Incremental Document Publish](Incremental_Document_Publish.md), parented to [Planned Features](../Planned_Features.md). It removes the parallel prepared-public document tree while retaining selected document/media publication and the existing queue JSON.

## Current And Next State

Status: implemented and cut over on 2026-10-16; active pending RGP.5 manual acceptance. The user authorised shared `draft: false` and the concrete metadata-only cutover. No test work ran within this delivery.

The duplicated `working/generated/publication/` tree and its consumers/initialiser are retired. Publish resolves selected ordinary/collection by-ID files directly and reads Selected, Recent and Search from their existing owners. Working builds public metadata beside management metadata. The reader no longer requires generated `content_url` fields.

The approved real-workspace cutover wrote five public metadata files, reduced private metadata to 244 referenced-media records plus the applied exclusion input, and removed transport URLs from the complete management index. No document bodies, assets or queues were written, and no Build, Search or Publish ran. No whole-corpus document equivalence claim is made.

Next: the user exercises normal operations and accepts the RGP.5 cases below. Static evidence and the metadata-only cutover do not establish Source Save, Full Build, withdrawal/restoration, diagram rendering or post-cutover Publish behavior. Git commit/push and deployment remain separate actions.

Working owns the Draft/unpublishable policy and its public metadata projection. Publish stays copy-only: it neither reads eligibility policy nor filters index/manifests. Document generation, exact dependency updates, referenced-media selection and explicit document withdrawals remain upstream. Folder-link handling and Selected eligibility belong to authoring under the responsibilities below.

## Requirements

- Remove `working/generated/publication/` and its consumers, duplicate document bodies, redundant shared copies, obsolete initialisation and separate-public-form readiness tracking. Retain the required public index/manifests alongside their management versions under the existing generated owners. Do not replace the retired tree with another parallel document tree or fallback reader.
- Use existing generated by-ID files for ordinary and collection document publication, including Catalogue. Resolve document and media locations through their configured owners; preserve portable document identities and `docs-media:` references without local/public URL rewriting. Retire redundant generated transport-URL metadata and reader prerequisites where confirmed unused by the identity-based provider.
- Build complete Working navigation/management manifests and their eligible public versions together at document build time. Reuse the metadata already loaded or produced by that build; public projection adds no second source-reading or document-rendering pass. Write and queue public index/manifests only when their projected contents change.
- Public ordinary navigation excludes Draft/unpublishable roots and their descendants without promoting excluded children. Public collection manifests exclude Draft rows and follow the eligibility of their configured ordinary host. Catalogue has fixed intrinsic document eligibility and follows the same host rule; host exclusion never withdraws Work JSON/media or deletes canonical Works.
- Use one Working-owned metadata eligibility selector for exact document effects and public list projection. Draft/unpublishable changes are resolved once and carried into both outputs. Downstream publication consumes completed files without authoring/schema/row audits, source/generated agreement checks or source-scan fallbacks.
- Working generation owns the saved index, selected management manifests, configured hosts and `working/source/unpublishable.json` needed for projection. Read required inputs once and carry their completed effects forward. Publish reads the queues and selected transfer inputs; it does not load management metadata or eligibility policy, project public lists, read Markdown, render documents, discover dependencies, produce media or reconcile complete corpora/destinations. Empty queues return before artifact/media setup or publication writes.
- Upstream operations continue queuing exact by-ID withdrawals/restorations and affected public metadata together. Removing a row from a public list does not remove the published document file. External policy changes still require owning generation to prepare the corresponding document/list effects; public metadata generation is not document reconciliation.
- Copy saved Selected JSON unchanged under the authoring contract below. Copy existing completed Recent/Search files unchanged when queued. Full Build retains Recent generation, Search retains its explicit generation owner, and ordinary operations do not add discovery freshness work.
- Preserve the agreed Docs/Catalogue queue structures, successful-unit removal, independent timestamps, selected media transfers and stop-and-report failures. Keep path/symlink confinement, required-input parsing and completed write/transfer verification. Do not add progress flags, retry guarantees, automatic repair, backups, full inventories or remote listings.
- Preserve the implemented Full Build boundary: no bulk Catalogue source loading, validation, stale-output discovery, rendering or Work queue contribution. Regenerate owns normal Catalogue generation/publication selections; explicit design maintenance owns complete Catalogue generation. Exact Catalogue dependencies remain document-only Docs selections.

### Public Metadata Updates

Draft and `unpublishable.json` are the eligibility inputs that can make public membership differ from the management view. Reuse the eligibility result when those inputs are unchanged; a document-body change alone does not require updating public index/manifests.

Changes to reader-visible metadata or structure, such as a title change, document creation/deletion or a move, still reach the corresponding public metadata during the same Working build. Only a changed projected result is written and queued. This keeps public lists current without redoing eligibility work or rewriting them for unrelated document changes; it does not change Full Build's general document/media queueing policy.

### Authoring Responsibilities

| Concern | Author responsibility | Application/publication boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Folder subjects and links | The user keeps documents with Folder subjects Draft and controls which authored local-folder content is publishable. | Ordinary Draft/unpublishable eligibility applies. Publish performs no Folder inspection, link scrubbing, automatic Draft enforcement or Folder-specific validation. |
| Selected Documents | The user ensures every starred document is publishable. | Star/Unstar and generation maintain the existing saved list. Publish copies that list unchanged, without eligibility filtering, membership audits or rejection of author choices. |
| Source and policy edits outside the app | The user runs the appropriate explicit generation before publication. | Owning generation supplies exact document/shared effects; Publish does not discover omitted changes. |
| Catalogue changes | The user completes Save, Refresh and Regenerate through their existing owners. | Full Build does not substitute for Catalogue generation. No new collection Draft/Delete UI or host-management workflow is introduced. |

The saved `working/source/selected.json` is an explicitly selected completed JSON transfer input. Copying it does not authorise reading Markdown or performing general authoring work during Publish. Folder and Selected responsibilities introduce no new runtime validation or workflow adjustment.

## Deliverables

| Artifact/owner | Target result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing ordinary/collection generated `by-id/` files | One document representation used by local readers and selected publication. No publication copy under Working. |
| Working index and `manage-manifest.json` files | Complete local authoring metadata, built alongside the eligible public views from the same metadata inputs. |
| Working public index and `manifest.json` files | Completed reader metadata produced at document build time; written and queued only when the projected contents change. No parallel document tree. |
| Preview public index and `manifest.json` files | Byte copies of queued completed Working public files, distributed without projection or filtering. |
| Existing Selected, Recent and Search files | Direct selected copies; no additional Working public variants. |
| Private generation metadata | Reuse the existing index, management manifests and Links records for their authoritative fields. Retain only concretely necessary media-reference/diagram preparation metadata under the existing generation owner; do not relocate the full duplicated `state.json` unchanged. Remove the separate-public-copy `public_ready` flag. |
| Queue handoffs and selected publishers | Existing JSON identities resolve the reused generated files and completed public metadata. Shared selections request copies without extending the queue schema. |
| Code/configuration/documentation cutover | Remove retired publication-tree readers/writers and initialisation after switching consumers. Preserve pending selections and timestamps; no blanket queue clearing, fallback aliases or shadow copies. |

Frontend ownership remains authoring choices, active-reader link/media resolution, local management presentation and one awaited Publish result. Python owns required Working generation, its public metadata projection and saved queue effects, confined filesystem writes and selected transfers. The delivery adds no authoring control, publication review modal or browser stage.

### Shared Document Choices

Agreed on 2026-10-16: retain the existing `draft` field in the common by-ID document. Eligible published documents carry `draft: false`; Catalogue continues omitting it. This explicitly changes the predecessor's public-field omission rule and avoids adding local metadata reads solely to remove one field from public JSON. Keep private collection authoring metadata in its existing management owner.

Diagram images now use externally authored SVG through the ordinary document-media workflow. The common by-ID payload supplies the same finished image references to local/public readers.

The common by-ID representation completes RGP.0.

## Process

1. Save, Rebuild, Import, eligibility/deletion operations and Regenerate complete their existing generated documents and known media/dependency effects. The same Working build maintains management metadata and eligible public index/manifests using the available metadata and Working-owned policy.
2. Working reuses unchanged eligibility, propagates changed public fields/structure and writes/queues only changed public index/manifests. Eligibility changes queue exact document withdrawals/restorations and affected lists together. Existing document/media queueing semantics and queue JSON remain unchanged.
3. Publish loads the queues and returns immediately if both are empty. It copies selected existing generated documents/media and completed public metadata into Preview, then distributes those bytes. It performs no policy reads, metadata projection or document generation. A queued removal uses its retained identity.
4. Publish removes each successful selection after its Preview/distribution unit completes. Selected, Recent and Search use their explicitly selected existing files without filtering or regeneration.
5. The first error stops the operation and reports the target/phase and completed effects. Diagnosis, correction and whether another Publish is appropriate remain manual.

## Follow-on

Changing Full Build's general document/media queueing to select only changed bytes, separating discovery refresh from Full Build, document-media cleanup and new publication eligibility rules remain separately scoped. This delivery limits changed-content queueing to public index/manifests and otherwise preserves the existing Full Build/Recent/Search operating choices while simplifying stored representations and selected publication.
